subject: Reserved capacity tenor & contingency — GPU-cost sensitivity
messages:
From: Alec Turner <alec.turner@skylinehealth.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Priya Shah <procurement@skylinehealth.ai>
Date: 2028-09-13T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — sizing + pricing sensitivity

Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo — Skyline Health is keen to move from pilot -> reserved capacity if we can get predictable unit economics. A few asks from procurement and finance:

- We want committed capacity for a 24–36 month tenor but need a pricing run that shows sensitivity to GPU market moves (both up and down).
- Can you outline how a price-protection corridor / indexation to market GPU spot pricing would look in your agreement?
- What discounts are available at different commit levels (e.g., 100k vGPU-hours/month vs 300k)? Who needs to approve >15% discounts?

Attached: initial-sizing-request.pdf (basic run rates).

Can we get a short walk-through and a draft term sheet by EOD Friday?

—Alec
Alec Turner
Head of AI Delivery, Skyline Health

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Alec Turner <alec.turner@skylinehealth.ai>, Priya Shah <procurement@skylinehealth.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-13T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — sizing + pricing sensitivity

Alec / Priya — thanks for the clear asks. High-level response and next steps below. I copied Karthik (pricing) and Marcus (dedicated ops) to align internally.

Summary (high level):
- Tenor: we can do 24 or 36 month commitments. Longer tenor increases ability to offer deeper tier discounts and burst credits.
- Pricing sensitivity approach: we propose a GPU-index corridor: a baseline unit rate with a +/- band tied to an agreed public GPU spot index; outside the band either party can trigger a review and an automatic credit/charge mechanism.
- Discounting: standard table (attached) shows volume bands: 0–99k vGPU-hrs: 10% off list; 100–249k: 13%; 250k+: 17%. Anything >18% requires Finance + CRO approval.

Requested from you: confirm target monthly vGPU-hours and preferred tenor (24 or 36). We will share a draft term sheet and a sizing matrix for you to review.

Attaching: redwood-sizing-matrix.xlsx (draft).

If that looks good I'll loop in Finance (David) for approval authority on one-off concessions and ask Pricing Ops for the corridor parameters.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-13T13:27:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Dedicated capacity ask — pricing sensitivity (internal)

Kimberly / Marcus — pulling some quick sensitivity numbers. Quoted text from Kimberly's outbound below.

Quick notes from pricing model (attached gpu-sensitivity-model.xlsx):
- Baseline: list unit $0.70 / vGPU-hr. Our current contracted long-term cost (fleet average) is ~$0.43 / vGPU-hr (weighted across NVL & A100 pools) but spot moves can swing +/- 30% in 6–12 months in stressed markets.
- Proposed corridor: +/- 10% annual corridor before trigger. If market average exceeds corridor for two consecutive months, automatic credit to customer equal to 50% of delta above corridor (to limit our downside) while also allowing an upper-charge if market moves > +12% (rare).
- Discount trade-offs: to offer 18%+ we need a blended commitment and a contractual opt-in to burst control (we can throttle non-critical burst for pilots), and Finance sign-off.

Request: David — can you confirm the approval threshold for one-off concessions and whether we can pre-authorize a 16% discount for SKY-9642 if they commit 300k+ vGPU-hrs for 36 months with a corridor and escrowed credits? If not, what's the process to get CRO sign-off?

(quoted) Kimberly wrote: "Discounting: standard table (attached) ... Anything >18% requires Finance + CRO approval."

Karthik
Senior Manager, Pricing & GTM Strategy

From: Alec Turner <alec.turner@skylinehealth.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Priya Shah <procurement@skylinehealth.ai>
Date: 2028-09-14T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — sizing + pricing sensitivity (Skyline counter)

Kimberly / team — appreciate the quick reply and model. Procurement has reviewed and proposes the following counterpoints:

1) Price: we are targeting a 20% discount at 300k+ vGPU-hrs for a 36-month tenor.
2) Corridor: we prefer a bilateral price-protection corridor (both directions) that settles via quarterly true-ups rather than discrete triggers so monthly volatility doesn't invoke churn.
3) Credits: if your unit costs move >+15% vs baseline, Skyline requests an automatic credits pool (applied to next quarter) equal to the excess above the 15% threshold up to a cap.

We can accept a managed-burst clause and operational throttles, but need governance (SLA + ops playbook + runbook) to be included in the term sheet.

Attaching: skyline-procurement-redlines.docx (procurement preferred language).

Can you come back with a firm term sheet and call out which specific approvals (names/roles) we need to execute quickly? Our timeline: Board review next week — need economics and draft contract by Thursday COB.

—Alec

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-14T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity ask — pricing sensitivity (internal decision)

Team — after reviewing Karthik's sensitivity model and Skyline's redlines, Finance (David) authorizes a one-time discretionary concession up to 16% for a 36-month commitment at >=300k vGPU-hrs provided we:

- Include a quarterly bilateral true-up mechanism (per Skyline request) with a +/- 12% corridor before credits apply.
- Put a credit cap equal to 3 months' committed spend and an escrow account for the first 12 months of the contract.
- Require an operational SLA appendix and runbook (Marcus to own) and a canary fallback to our hosted tier for first 90 days.

Important: any concession >16% will require CRO sign-off and legal to accept the redline language. Kimberly — please draft a term sheet reflecting the 16% concession, the corridor/true-up mechanics, and the escrow language. Share with David for countersign and I'll prepare the exec memo for CRO if they push beyond 16%.
